facts.fact: Gen Z voters are defined by the page as those born between 1997 and 2012.
facts.quote: Gen Z voters (born 1997 to 2012) are now the second-largest voting bloc in America

facts.fact: According to Nielsen's Gauge report (third-party), adults 18 to 24 spend over 40% of their TV time on streaming platforms.
facts.quote: According to Nielsen's Gauge report, adults 18 to 24 spend over 40% of their TV time on streaming platforms.

facts.fact: Per the page, cable and broadcast together account for less than a third of 18-to-24-year-olds' TV viewing time.
facts.quote: Cable and broadcast together account for less than a third of their viewing.

facts.fact: The page states that the average time spent on a social media ad is under two seconds (no source cited).
facts.quote: The average time spent on a social media ad is under two seconds.

facts.fact: The vendor states that a 30-second CTV ad on a streaming platform gets a 90%+ completion rate (vendor's own claim, no source cited).
facts.quote: A 30-second [CTV ad](https://adwave.com/resources/what-is-connected-tv-advertising) on a streaming platform gets a 90%+ completion rate.

facts.fact: Adwave states that campaigns can run across 100+ streaming channels simultaneously without negotiating individual platform deals (vendor's own claim).
facts.quote: campaigns can run across 100+ streaming channels simultaneously, reaching Gen Z wherever they watch without having to negotiate individual platform deals.

facts.fact: The page recommends starting CTV campaigns targeting Gen Z 8 to 12 weeks before a primary.
facts.quote: Start CTV campaigns targeting Gen Z 8 to 12 weeks before the primary.

facts.fact: CTV age targeting options offered by platforms are 18 to 29 for broad Gen Z reach or 18 to 24 for the youngest eligible voters.
facts.quote: Target 18 to 29 for the broadest Gen Z reach, or narrow to 18 to 24 for the youngest eligible voters.

facts.fact: The page says smart TVs are the fastest-growing streaming device among 18 to 29 year olds, citing Nielsen data, but gives no growth figure.
facts.quote: Nielsen data shows that smart TVs are the fastest-growing device for streaming among 18 to 29 year olds.

facts.fact: Research from the Video Advertising Bureau (third-party) reportedly shows even younger viewers perceive TV advertising as more trustworthy than social media ads; no figure is given.
facts.quote: research from the Video Advertising Bureau shows that even younger viewers perceive TV advertising as more trustworthy than social media ads.

facts.fact: In the awareness phase (12 to 8 weeks before a general election), the page recommends allocating 30% of total CTV spend.
facts.quote: Phase 1 (12 to 8 weeks out): Awareness.** Introduce the candidate and core platform. Focus on issue-based messaging that establishes relevance to Gen Z voters. Budget allocation: 30% of total CTV spend.

facts.fact: In the persuasion phase (8 to 4 weeks before a general election), the page recommends allocating 40% of total CTV spend.
facts.quote: Phase 2 (8 to 4 weeks out): Persuasion.** Shift to comparison and contrast messaging. Address specific policy differences on issues Gen Z cares about. Budget allocation: 40% of total CTV spend.

facts.fact: In the mobilization phase (final 4 weeks), the page recommends allocating 30% of total CTV spend.
facts.quote: Phase 3 (final 4 weeks): Mobilization.** Pivot to get-out-the-vote messaging. Focus on voter registration deadlines, early voting dates, and polling locations. Budget allocation: 30% of total CTV spend.

facts.fact: For Gen Z voter targeting, the page recommends a frequency of 8 to 12 impressions per household over the campaign period.
facts.quote: aim for a frequency of 8 to 12 impressions per household over the campaign period.

facts.fact: The page states that CTV campaigns typically drive 15 to 30% increases in direct and organic website traffic during active flights.
facts.unit: % increase in direct and organic traffic
facts.quote: CTV campaigns typically drive 15 to 30% increases in direct and organic traffic during active flights.

facts.fact: The page recommends a total CTV budget of $2,000 to $10,000 for local races such as city council, school board, or county campaigns.
facts.quote: Recommended CTV budget:** $2,000 to $10,000 total for the campaign cycle

facts.fact: For local races, the page estimates reach of 10,000 to 50,000 Gen Z households in targeted areas.
facts.quote: Reach:** 10,000 to 50,000 Gen Z households in targeted areas

facts.fact: For local races, the page recommends a flight of 6 to 8 weeks before election day.
facts.quote: Flight:** 6 to 8 weeks before election day

facts.fact: Adwave's minimum spend is $30 a day, according to the page.
facts.quote: With [Adwave's $30-a-day minimum](https://adwave.com/pricing), even first-time candidates can test CTV before committing larger budgets

facts.fact: The page recommends a total CTV budget of $10,000 to $50,000 for state legislative races.
facts.quote: Recommended CTV budget:** $10,000 to $50,000 total

facts.fact: For state legislative races, the page estimates reach of 50,000 to 200,000 Gen Z households across the district.
facts.quote: Reach:** 50,000 to 200,000 Gen Z households across the district

facts.fact: For state legislative races, the page recommends a flight of 8 to 12 weeks before election day.
facts.quote: Flight:** 8 to 12 weeks before election day

facts.fact: The page recommends a total CTV budget of $50,000 to $250,000+ for congressional and statewide races.
facts.quote: Recommended CTV budget:** $50,000 to $250,000+ total

facts.fact: For congressional and statewide races, the page estimates reach of 200,000 to 1 million+ Gen Z households.
facts.quote: Reach:** 200,000 to 1 million+ Gen Z households

facts.fact: For congressional and statewide races, the page recommends a flight of 12 to 16 weeks before election day.
facts.quote: Flight:** 12 to 16 weeks before election day with phased messaging

facts.fact: The page states that completion rates for CTV ads on streaming services exceed 90%.
facts.quote: Completion rates exceed 90%, meaning nearly every viewer watches the full ad.

facts.fact: The page gives CTV CPMs for political advertising as typically ranging from $20 to $40.
facts.quote: CTV CPMs for political advertising typically range from $20 to $40, depending on targeting specificity and market competition.

facts.fact: The page says campaigns that paired CTV with text-based outreach reported text response rates 2 to 3 times higher when recipients had seen the TV ads first.
facts.quote: text response rates were 2 to 3 times higher when recipients had been exposed to the candidate's TV ads first.

facts.fact: Campaigns focused on fewer Gen Z households at 10+ impressions per household reportedly outperformed those spreading budget across wider audiences, per the page.
facts.quote: Campaigns that focused budget on reaching fewer Gen Z households more frequently (10+ impressions per household) outperformed

facts.fact: The page advises starting CTV ads targeting Gen Z at least 8 weeks before election day, or 12 weeks for competitive races.
facts.quote: Start at least 8 weeks before election day for awareness building. For competitive races, 12 weeks is better.

facts.fact: State legislative candidates who began CTV 10+ weeks before election day saw measurably higher name recognition among voters under 30 than those running only in the final three weeks, per the page.
facts.unit: weeks before election day or earlier
facts.quote: State legislative candidates who started CTV campaigns 10+ weeks before election day saw measurably higher name recognition among voters under 30

facts.fact: The page states that a local campaign can reach meaningful Gen Z voter reach with $2,000 to $5,000 in CTV spend.
facts.quote: Most local campaigns find that $2,000 to $5,000 in CTV provides meaningful reach among Gen Z voters in their district.

facts.fact: The page states that TikTok does not accept political ads.
facts.quote: (TikTok does not accept political ads.)
